security_privacy_cost_impact: A new write path: an owner, after step-up, can move their own active workspace to closing and back, through a SECURITY DEFINER command owned by app_command, audited in the same transaction; a refused audit write aborts the action. app_command gains its first grants (USAGE on app; SELECT (id, lifecycle_state) and UPDATE (lifecycle_state, updated_by) on app.workspaces; INSERT on app.audit_logs; EXECUTE on six functions owned by app_authz: jwt_subject, is_active_member, workspace_member_role, acting_user_admits_business, acting_user_admits_page and jwt_aal (corrected in the review round, A1 F4, Q0 F6)), each pinned. app_authz gains five column reads of workspace_member_scopes and an own-rows policy. The actor is bound to request.jwt.claims (RFC-2026-023 §4 and RFC-2026-026 §3.3/1's residual: a session that sets the claims and can execute a command writes as anyone it names; EXECUTE on the commands is authenticated's alone). Refusals about a workspace the actor is not an active member of are unrecorded (Q-026-10 (iii)). Any active member can cause a refusal row at will (A1 F1): since the review round the command refuses request_id and correlation_id outside 1-128 characters of [A-Za-z0-9._:-] with 22023, so free text, an e-mail address or 100,000 characters no longer reach the append-only log; a digit string of an ID number's shape still fits, and a table CHECK and a rate limit are owed (open_blockers[200] (11)). A logical-replication subscription, which writes audit rows past every policy and trigger, is now refused by the producer rule (A1 F2). The batch's own fixtures carry no secret and no PII; no network, no cost.
migration_and_data_impact: One forward migration, 172_acting_user_and_closing_command.sql; no table, column or data change. Four earlier apply-time blocks superseded with additive final-state replacements. The snapshot declares 172 not applied. No open_blockers line moves (the manifest's amendment list keeps four paths; [200] is added at the end).

The isolation runner gains `after` reads and four identities; existing cases are unchanged.
known_limitations: The step-up claim and function ownership under a non-superuser applier are not measured on the platform (open_blockers[200] (2), [199] (e)).

§8.1/1 drift 16 (an operator or aggregate over a producer) cannot be built against three-argument producers, and drift 12 (the reader rules) is vacuous while the reader list is empty; the cast drift (20) and BEGIN ATOMIC at every level in the driver are owed (open_blockers[195]).

audit-producer-rule part (i), widened in the review round, refuses any function or view, whatever its owner or security, that names app.workspaces unless it is one of the two lifecycle functions or the pinned reader app.workspace_member_role(uuid): stricter than RFC-2026-023 §8/3's 'writes' about reads, and blind to a route through dynamic SQL only as far as part (c), which refuses it. Its first form was blind to calls (C0 M1).
The full `try-it demo` was not run: the tool refuses this run's only port.

RFC-2026-026 §8.1/5 for the closing command is asserted by 172's check 7, but 170's block holds the same property first, so no drift appended to 140 reaches check 7 itself.

The pinned grant probe reads app and private only; app_command's privileges anywhere are held by 172's widened check 3, but a view outside app and private granted to app_worker or app_maintenance is held by nothing named here (open_blockers[200] (15)).
No CHECK bounds request_id or correlation_id on app.audit_logs itself (it would narrow CTR-AUD-001); the bound is in the two command bodies (open_blockers[200] (11)).
